title: Fix lock PID-write exception cleanup with independent clean-path and orphan regression fixtures
instructions: A INTEGRATION, EXACT base_sha; this replaces failed task A-20261028-lock-pid-write-cleanup-0753-01, which failed because its generated test PRECREATED an orphan .lock then expected an ENOSPC os.write: O_EXCL necessarily timed out first. Implement only the source-confirmed ArchiveWriterLock.__enter__ cleanup gap in storage.py: when THIS acquisition successfully created the lock but writing the owner PID raises OSError, close fd, remove ONLY this newly-created lock (compare inode/dev with fstat/lstat where practical), and re-raise original OSError; NEVER delete preexisting locks, never auto-reap unknown crash orphans; preserve FileExistsError timeout fail-closed and existing APIs. Test MUST be TWO SEPARATE test functions with INDEPENDENT tmp_path archives, not one combined fixture: (1) test_pid_write_failure_removes_only_new_lock: start with assert not lock_path.exists(); monkeypatch storage.os.write narrowly to raise OSError(errno.ENOSPC,'simulated PID write failure') during ArchiveWriterLock.__enter__; assert errno == errno.ENOSPC, no newly created .lock remains; restore monkeypatch before a second successful lock acquisition, assert lock removed after exit. CRITICAL: DO NOT CREATE A LOCK BEFORE THE ENOSPC TEST, or the PID write is unreachable. (2) test_preexisting_orphan_lock_is_preserved: use a DIFFERENT archive path and create .lock with fixed sentinel text, NO os.write patch; assert TimeoutError from ArchiveWriterLock(timeout=0.05,poll_interval=0.005) and exact sentinel unchanged; cleanup only test-created fixture in finally. Keep tests deterministic, offline, no sleep as sole oracle; preserve existing reader/writer visibility and orphan-crash behavior. Before commit run python -m py_compile on both changed files, git diff --check, all three listed pytest commands in order with zero exit status (targeted then FULL Capital Flow); no code push on failure, no broad redesign.
